To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the normal metal in between ferromagnetic and superconducting layers can lead to spontaneous currents in such systems and that this effect is periodic with the thickness of normal metal.

the spontaneous currents can be induced in the ferromagnet - superconductor - normal metal system; the spontaneous currents can flow in opposite directions in the same system; the spontaneous current can be switched periodically by varying the thickness of the intermediate normal layer.
the inclusion of a normal metal layer between ferromagnet/superconductor leads to the suppression of spontaneous currents in a trilayer.

the interplay between the superconducting and magnetic properties in hybrid structures and with the spontaneous currents in such systems.
the properties of the system in which the proximity effect is mediated by a normal metal layer.

the inclusion of a normal metal layer in a ferromagnetic–superconductor system can be used as a means to switch the current in the system.
the normal metal layer does not necessarily suppress the spontaneous current state in a F– N– S structure, but rather can lead to a periodic switching of this state.
a normal metal sandwich in between ferromagnetic and superconducting materials can lead to a rich variety of ground states and can also be used to control the spontaneous current flow.

the inclusion of a normal metal slab between the ferromagnet and the superconductor can lead to a rich variety of ground state properties.
